newsitem.title: USA: 3M posts record profits but still short of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: 3M posts record profits but still short of forecasts.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co. Wednesday reported record sales and profits for the second quarter but its results still fell short of Wall Street's expectations and the company's stock lost ground.
3M said its earnings rose 10 percent to $418 million, or $1.01 a share, on sales of $3.8 billion, vs. year-earlier earnings of $381 million, or 91 cents a share, on sales of $3.5 billion.
But the results were below analysts' estimates of $1.03 a share, and 3M's stock lost $3 before trimming its loss to $1.06 at $99.25 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The company, which make recording tapes, abrasives, speciality chemicals and health care products, said it was still on target to post record 1997 results despite the effects of the strong dollar, which reduced its second-quarter sales by nearly 4 percent.
"Looking ahead, we expect our solid performance to continue in the second half of this year," said L.D. DeSimone, chairman and chief executive.

"While the stronger U.S. dollar will continue to impact us, we are on track to deliver record 1997 results as we continue to implement our growth initiatives in the United States and abroad," he said.
In the United States, sales were up 10 percent to $1.8 billion, and internationally, sales topped $2 billion for the first time despite a 7 percent negative currency effect, the company said.
